observation.goal: Verify the counter page at http://127.0.0.1:3000 starts at Count: 0, then click Increment five times and enter Mend to observe Count: 5 and Hello, Mend!.
observation.result: Opened Chromium at http://127.0.0.1:3000 and inspected its screenshot: the page initially displayed Count: 0 and Hello, world! with an empty Name input. Clicked Increment five times and typed Mend into Name. The resulting screenshot visibly displayed Count: 5, the input value Mend, and Hello, Mend!. No failures observed.

observation.goal: Verify the desktop counter reads 2 and Hello, Claude!
observation.result: Opened http://127.0.0.1:6090/demo in the desktop Chromium. The page title is "Mend desktop check". The counter started at "Count: 0". The increment button is labeled "Add one", not "Increment". Clicked it twice; the counter read "Count: 1" then "Count: 2". Clicked the "Your name" field and typed "Claude". The page then showed the greeting "Hello, Claude" below the field. Final screenshot: Count: 2 and "Hello, Claude" are both visible. PARTIAL MISMATCH with the goal: the greeting has no exclamation mark. The page source builds it as "Hello, " + the input value, so "Hello, Claude!" is never rendered. Counter check passed; greeting text differs from the expected "Hello, Claude!" by the missing "!".

observation.goal: Verify takeover aborts active desktop code without stopping the coding agent

takeover.diagnostic: A controlled workspace HTTP probe ran a code worker with six 5-second waits. Takeover aborted it with HTTP 400 and The operation was aborted. The primary coding process remained alive. This was a controller diagnostic, not another provider-driven task.
